title: The map from extension by zero to direct image is injective
statement: Let $\pi:U\to X$ be a finite etale morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $\Lambda$ a commutative ring and $M$ a sheaf of $\Lambda_U$-modules on $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $c_M:\pi_!M\to\pi_*M$ be the canonical map from extension by zero to direct image [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-to-star-map]. Then for every object $W$ of $X_{\Et}$ the map $c_M(W):(\pi_!M)(W)\to(\pi_*M)(W)$ is injective; in particular $c_M$ is a monomorphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules. Equivalently, the presheaf map $c^p_M:P_M\to\pi_*M$ of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map] is locally injective: if $x=\sum_{i=1}^n s_{\varphi_i}\in P_M(V)$ ($\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_n$ distinct $X$-morphisms $V\to U$, $s_{\varphi_i}\in M(V,\varphi_i)$) has $c^p_{M,V}(x)=0$, then there is a covering $\{V_k\to V\}$ of $V$ in $X_{\Et}$ on whose members $x$ restricts to $0$ (in fact one may take $V$ partitioned into finitely many open and closed pieces on each of which every two $\varphi_i$ either agree or have disjoint graphs).

proof.text: *Coincidence loci.* Notation as in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map]: for an object $V$ of $X_{\Et}$, $V_U=V\times_XU$ with projections $p_V,q_V$, and for an $X$-morphism $\varphi:V\to U$ the graph $\Gamma_\varphi=(\mathrm{id}_V,\varphi):V\to V_U$, so $p_V\Gamma_\varphi=\mathrm{id}_V$, $q_V\Gamma_\varphi=\varphi$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\varphi,\psi:V\to U$ be $X$-morphisms and $E=\Gamma_\varphi^{-1}(\Gamma_\psi(V))\subseteq V$. Claim: (a) $E$ is open and closed in $V$; (b) if $u:E\to V$ is the inclusion of the open subscheme $E$, then $\varphi u=\psi u$; (c) if $v\in V$, $w\in V$ and $\Gamma_\varphi(v)=\Gamma_\psi(w)$, then $v=w\in E$. Proof: (a) $\Gamma_\psi(V)$ is open and closed in $V_U$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map(1)] and $\Gamma_\varphi$ is continuous. (c) Apply $p_V$: $v=p_V\Gamma_\varphi(v)=p_V\Gamma_\psi(w)=w$, and then $\Gamma_\varphi(v)\in\Gamma_\psi(V)$, i.e. $v\in E$. (b) Let $O=\Gamma_\psi(V)$, an open subscheme of $V_U$ with inclusion $j_O$, and $\gamma:V\to O$ the isomorphism with $j_O\gamma=\Gamma_\psi$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map(1)]. Since $\Gamma_\varphi u(E)\subseteq O$ as sets, $\Gamma_\varphi u=j_O h$ for a unique morphism $h:E\to O$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. Put $g=\gamma^{-1}h:E\to V$; then $\Gamma_\varphi u=j_O\gamma g=\Gamma_\psi g$, and applying $p_V$ gives $u=g$. Hence $\Gamma_\varphi u=\Gamma_\psi u$, and applying $q_V$ gives $\varphi u=\psi u$. (This is the Stacks remark that the pairwise equalizers of the $\varphi_i$ are open and closed in $V$, here derived from the open and closed graphs, for finite etale $\pi$.)

*Refining $V$ by clopen pieces.* Let $V$ be an object of $X_{\Et}$ and $x=\sum_{i=1}^n s_{\varphi_i}\in P_M(V)$ with $\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_n$ distinct $X$-morphisms $V\to U$ and $s_{\varphi_i}\in M(V,\varphi_i)$ (every element of $P_M(V)=\bigoplus_{\varphi}M(V,\varphi)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] has this form). For $i<j$ let $E_{ij}=\Gamma_{\varphi_i}^{-1}(\Gamma_{\varphi_j}(V))$, open and closed in $V$ by step 1(a), and put $E^1_{ij}=E_{ij}$, $E^0_{ij}=V\setminus E_{ij}$. For each function $\varepsilon$ from the set of pairs $i<j$ to $\{0,1\}$ let $V_\varepsilon=\bigcap_{i<j}E^{\varepsilon(i,j)}_{ij}$: finitely many open and closed subsets of $V$, pairwise disjoint, with union $V$ (each point lies in exactly one $E^0_{ij}$ or $E^1_{ij}$ for each pair). Regard $V_\varepsilon$ as an open subscheme with inclusion $u_\varepsilon:V_\varepsilon\to V$, an open immersion, hence etale, so $V_\varepsilon\to V\to X$ is etale and $u_\varepsilon$ is a morphism of $X_{\Et}$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation(1),(2)]; the family $\{u_\varepsilon\}_\varepsilon$ is jointly surjective, hence a covering of $V$ in $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. On $V'=V_\varepsilon$ with $u=u_\varepsilon$, for every pair $i<j$: if $\varepsilon(i,j)=1$ then $\varphi_iu=\varphi_ju$, because $u$ factors through the open subscheme $E_{ij}$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] and step 1(b) applies; if $\varepsilon(i,j)=0$ then $\Gamma_{\varphi_iu}(V')\cap\Gamma_{\varphi_ju}(V')=\varnothing$ in $V'_U$: the induced morphism $u_U=u\times_X\mathrm{id}_U:V'_U\to V_U$ satisfies $u_U\Gamma_{\varphi u}=\Gamma_\varphi u$ for every $\varphi$ (both have components $u$ and $\varphi u$ [def-pc-fibre-product]), so $\Gamma_{\varphi_iu}(a)=\Gamma_{\varphi_ju}(b)$ would give $\Gamma_{\varphi_i}(u(a))=\Gamma_{\varphi_j}(u(b))$, hence $u(a)\in E_{ij}$ by step 1(c), contradicting $u(a)\in V_\varepsilon\subseteq V\setminus E_{ij}$. Consequently, for $X$-morphisms $\psi=\varphi_iu$ and $\psi'=\varphi_ju$ on $V'$, either $\psi=\psi'$ or $\Gamma_\psi(V')\cap\Gamma_{\psi'}(V')=\varnothing$ (if $V'=\varnothing$ both hold trivially).

*$c^p_M$ is locally injective.* Let $x\in P_M(V)$ as in step 2 with $c^p_{M,V}(x)=\sum_ie_{\varphi_i}(s_{\varphi_i})=0$ in $M(V_U,q_V)=(\pi_*M)(V)$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map(3), def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. We show $x|_{V'}=0$ for each piece $V'=V_\varepsilon$, $u=u_\varepsilon$, of step 2; since these form a covering of $V$, this proves local injectivity. By the restriction maps of $P_M$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map(3), def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension], $x|_{V'}$ has in the summand of $\psi$ the entry $t_\psi=\sum_{i:\varphi_iu=\psi}M(u)(s_{\varphi_i})\in M(V',\psi)$; let $\psi_1,\dots,\psi_m$ be the distinct morphisms among $\varphi_1u,\dots,\varphi_nu$, so $x|_{V'}=\sum_at_{\psi_a}$ and, by step 2, the open and closed subsets $O_a=\Gamma_{\psi_a}(V')$ of $V'_U$ are pairwise disjoint. As $c^p_M$ is a morphism of presheaves [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map(3)], $\sum_ae_{\psi_a}(t_{\psi_a})=c^p_{M,V'}(x|_{V'})=c^p_{M,V}(x)|_{V'}=0$ in $M(V'_U)$. Fix $b$. For $a\neq b$, $O_b\subseteq V'_U\setminus O_a$, and $e_{\psi_a}(t_{\psi_a})$ restricts to $0$ on $V'_U\setminus O_a$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map(2)], hence to $0$ on $O_b$ (restriction along the open immersions $O_b\subseteq V'_U\setminus O_a\subseteq V'_U$, morphisms of $U_{\Et}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation(1),(2)]). So $e_{\psi_b}(t_{\psi_b})|_{O_b}=0$. Since $\Gamma_{\psi_b}$ factors through the open subscheme $O_b$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map(1)], $t_{\psi_b}=M(\Gamma_{\psi_b})(e_{\psi_b}(t_{\psi_b}))$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map(2)] is a restriction of $e_{\psi_b}(t_{\psi_b})|_{O_b}=0$, so $t_{\psi_b}=0$. Hence $x|_{V'}=0$. (Stacks: 'by the disjointness of the supports of these sections ... $s'_{\varphi_i}=0$ for each $i$, whence $s_{\varphi_i}=0$'.)

*Conclusion.* By [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-to-star-map], $\pi_!M=P_M^\#$ is the sheafification of the presheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules $P_M$ with map $\eta_M$, $\pi_*M$ is a sheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules, and $c_M$ is the unique morphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules with $c_M\circ\eta_M=c^p_M$. By step 3, $c^p_M$ is locally injective on the site $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] (for $c^p_{M,V}(x)=0$, $x$ restricts to $0$ on the covering $\{V_\varepsilon\to V\}$). Hence [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-sheafification-lift-injective], applied with $\mathcal C=X_{\Et}$, $\mathcal O=\Lambda_X$, $\mathcal P=P_M$, $\mathcal F=\pi_*M$, $f=c^p_M$, gives that $c_M(W)$ is injective for every object $W$ of $X_{\Et}$ and that $c_M$ is a monomorphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. (Stacks states this for separated etale $j$; a finite morphism is separated, but the argument above uses separatedness only through the open and closed graphs of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map(1)].)
